notes: Coordinates are original pixels of p29_ddf5dc.jpg (2500 x 1875) unless an element / also entry names another photo. downhill_img = unit vector in image axes (x right, y down) pointing down the slope as seen in plan.

Reading rules used on p29: the sun is at the image TOP (north): planes facing up-image are bright (lum ~150-170), facing down-image dark (~90-115), sideways ~130-150 (attrs.lum = mean grey of the plane). Dark cap-shingle lines = ridges / hips; bright white / silver lines = open metal valleys or the white gutter / fascia line of an eave (an eave line drawn over another roof = upper eave over a lower roof); rakes of gable ends are white trim.

p29 is near-nadir but NOT orthographic: the drone is roughly above the image centre (~1250, 940), so high points are displaced away from it (up-left for most of this house) by roughly 5-7 px per metre of height. Ridges and two-storey eaves therefore sit up-left of their plan position relative to one-storey roofs, hips are not at exactly 45 deg, and a lower roof is partly hidden under the upper eave on the up-left sides and over-exposed on the down-right sides (e.g. the north porch NCP shows as a 10-20 px strip only).

Scale at roof level from the PV panels (~1.0 x 1.7 m): about 31-36 px/m (panel short side 31 px; long sides 51-64 px, foreshortened on the sloping planes). Pitch not measurable from the nadir view; the front gables in hero / p01 suggest ~6-7.5/12 (27-32 deg); the core deck is near flat.

Plan logic: the two-storey core is one big hip-roof mass whose footprint is chamfered at 45 deg on the SW (front / entry), NE and SE; its top is a flat membrane deck (pentagon dA-dB-dC-dD-dE). The 45-deg planes obey the expected intersection rules (NE/SE hip horizontal, SW/NW valley horizontal, SE/SW valley vertical in plan), which supports the reading.

Wings off the core: NC (N, hip, shares the east plane with CC), BG (E, gable over the balcony), WW (W, hip with a narrower west cross gable), FG (SW front gable over the entry), BC (S, hip with a south gable bump). One-storey: garage wing (NW), north wing with the stone chimney (N), covered patio PB (SE, toward the pool), wraparound porch (W / SW / S / E) and the north porch.

The front of the house faces SW (the front lawns at the lower left): entry under FG on the 45-deg facade, the porch wrapping left (south of the west wing) and right (west of the south block) - matches p01 / hero. p28 looks from the NE (over the play area) at the pool side: from its left to right it shows PB + EP + BC (south chimney), BG (balcony gable with a4), NC with the NCP porch corner post and the north chimney, then the north wing (a2) and the garage wing (a1).

Roofing: dark charcoal architectural asphalt shingles everywhere except the low-slope deck (dark membrane); white / cream fascia and gutters; open metal (silver) valleys; dark ridge / hip caps. Craftsman details from the front photos: exposed rafter tails, knee-brace brackets under the gable rakes, shingled gable faces with louvered vents.
Solar: six arrays, 50 panels total, all on planes facing N, W, E or NE (none on the south faces); the listing says 50 panels, so the count is complete.

No dormers, crickets or balconies cut into the roof are visible; the upstairs balcony is under the BG gable roof (open east end). A satellite dish is wall-mounted on the north face of NC (p28), not on the roof.
open_questions: NW wing junction (G_N / T1 / GE_n / GE_s / CW_N / CW_S, around (415-445, 440-560)): which ridge is higher, garage wing or north wing? The short dark lines meeting at (442,490) and the parallel hip + white-valley pairs fit two crossing hip roofs of similar height, but perspective (~40 px between ridge and eave level here) makes the exact topology uncertain; the north wing could also be a taller one-storey room.
Storeys of the north wing CW (with the stone chimney): read as one storey from p28 (its eave is below NC eaves, bins / AC at its wall), but the wing is wide (N-S ~11-12 m) for a one-storey hip.

Depth of the hidden one-storey roofs under two-storey eaves: north porch NCP (p28 shows a full porch with a corner post, p29 only 10-20 px), and how far the north wing CW_N and patio PB_N run in under the core eaves.
Exact form of the small entry-porch gable over the front steps on the SW porch leg (hero / p01) - barely separable in p29.
Deck: height relative to the CC ridge (the CC south hip-end drains onto it, the surrounding planes start at its edges, so it sits just below the CC ridge) and its drainage direction.
Array a4 panels (and the landscape panel of a1) look pale in p29 but dark PV in p28 - assumed PV (the 50-panel total only works if they are PV).
Eave overhang depths and gutter presence on every eave are not measurable from p29 (white lines are visible along almost all eaves; they may be fascia rather than gutters).
